scope: Verified U.S. private-sector proposals stopped through a local denial, withdrawal, or prohibition after documented public opposition. Inclusion records disposition; it does not by itself establish a causal economic effect.
selection_basis: A case requires a named proposal, a defensible location, a dated disposition, and linked evidence for both the government or developer action and the public-opposition context. Relocation, redesign, litigation, and weak post-decision windows remain explicit.

projects.name: Nestlé Cascade Locks Bottling Plant
projects.decision_label: County voters prohibited commercial water bottling
projects.summary: A proposed bottled-water plant was stopped after Hood River County voters adopted a commercial water-bottling prohibition. This cross-sector case provides a longer post-decision window but is not a data-center analogue.
projects.proposal_description: Nestlé sought to develop a bottling operation in Cascade Locks using spring water associated with a proposed water-right exchange. The proposal became a countywide dispute over public water, employment, and local control.

proposed_scale.label: Proposed water use
proposed_scale.value: More than 100 million gallons per year discussed in the proposal

projects.site_afterlife: Parcel-level reuse has not yet been established in this dataset. Current Port of Cascade Locks tenant information documents continuing industrial activity in the community but is not treated as proof of reuse of the exact proposed parcel.
projects.evidence_note: Cross-sector comparison. The longer post-period is useful descriptively, but differences in water use, labor, utilities, and tax treatment prevent a direct one-for-one comparison with a data center.

timeline.title: Independent preliminary review describes the proposal
timeline.summary: An Oregon State University report summarized the proposed facility, water exchange, and open economic and environmental questions.

timeline.title: County voters adopt water-bottling prohibition
timeline.summary: The countywide vote prohibited commercial water bottling and stopped the proposed plant from proceeding on its planned basis.

timeline.title: Community-level activity is documented; parcel reuse remains unresolved
timeline.summary: The port lists current industrial tenants, including pFriem operations, but this release does not equate those premises with the exact Nestlé proposal site.

projects.name: Catlett Data Center Campus
projects.summary: The applicant withdrew a rezoning for a large data-center campus after organized opposition. Later warehouse preapplication activity means the site should be tracked as redesigned, not treated as permanently undeveloped.
projects.proposal_description: The application sought to rezone roughly 60 acres in the Catlett Service District for a multi-building data-center campus and associated electrical infrastructure.

proposed_scale.label: Proposed campus
proposed_scale.value: Approximately 1.4 million square feet on 60 acres

projects.site_afterlife: Fauquier reporting identifies later preapplication material for a non-distributing warehouse concept. The site is therefore classified as redesigned rather than a clean no-development outcome.
projects.evidence_note: The official record verifies withdrawal. Advocacy reporting supports a contributing community role, while the exact causal weight of opposition versus applicant economics remains unquantified.

timeline.summary: County materials describe a request to rezone 60 acres for data-center uses in the Catlett Service District.

timeline.title: County agenda records application withdrawal
timeline.summary: The Planning Commission agenda was amended to reflect withdrawal of the rezoning and special-exception applications.

timeline.title: Warehouse concept appears in preapplication material
timeline.summary: A later non-distributing warehouse concept indicates potential redesign of the site rather than a stable untreated parcel.

projects.name: AWS Third Louisa County Campus
projects.summary: AWS withdrew a third Louisa County campus application after public resistance. Two other AWS campuses continued, making this a within-county siting contrast rather than a county without data-center investment.
projects.proposal_description: AWS applied for a conditional-use permit for a third campus concept in Louisa County. The proposal was materially larger than a single building and sat within a county already hosting other AWS development.
projects.site_afterlife: No verified alternative use for the exact proposed site is published here. Other AWS campuses in Louisa County remain separate operating-project observations.
projects.evidence_note: This is not a never-treated county. Any causal design must separate the rejected third campus from other AWS and EdgeCore activity in the same county.

timeline.title: AWS files for a third campus
timeline.summary: Louisa County materials identify a conditional-use application for another campus concept.

timeline.title: Residents organize against the proposal
timeline.summary: Public reporting documented strong resistance during the application period.

timeline.title: AWS withdraws the application
timeline.summary: The third-campus application was withdrawn before approval.

timeline.title: County remains exposed to other data-center development
timeline.summary: The rejected proposal must be analyzed alongside the county's other active campus projects, not as removal of the entire sector.

projects.name: Provident Brassie Data Center
projects.summary: Provident withdrew its former Brassie Golf Course data-center proposal after resident opposition and the Town Council declared the scale and location unacceptable. Subsequent planning shifted toward other development concepts.
projects.proposal_description: Provident proposed eight large data-center buildings and related generator, switching, and substation areas on and near the former Brassie Golf Course property.
projects.site_afterlife: Town records in 2025 describe the development team shifting away from a data center and soliciting community input on a future development opportunity. The final alternative use is not yet fixed in this release.
projects.evidence_note: The developer withdrawal and council position are primary-record facts. The site is classified as redesigned because development planning continued after the data-center concept ended.

timeline.summary: Provident presented a multi-building data-center concept for the former golf-course property.

timeline.title: Town Council rejects the proposal's scale and location
timeline.summary: The council said it could not support the project at its current scale and location and required extensive further review if pursued.

timeline.title: Provident formally withdraws both petitions
timeline.summary: The developer withdrew the planned-unit-development and annexation petitions.

timeline.title: Town solicits input on a different development opportunity
timeline.summary: The former Brassie property remained in planning, so the case is tracked as a redesign rather than permanent nondevelopment.

projects.name: Etheridge Lakes Data Center
projects.summary: Chesapeake City Council unanimously denied the Etheridge Lakes rezoning after extensive public comment and an earlier Planning Commission recommendation against it.
projects.proposal_description: The applicant sought to rezone a 22.6-acre parcel near Centerville Turnpike and Etheridge Manor Boulevard for a two-story data center.
projects.site_afterlife: No verified replacement development on the parcel is published here. Chesapeake subsequently developed broader data-center policy, a distinct citywide outcome that should not be confused with parcel reuse.
projects.evidence_note: The denial is final for the reviewed rezoning. Community testimony is well documented, but the record also cites land-use compatibility and availability of other viable uses.

timeline.title: Rezoning application begins review
timeline.summary: The city opened review of a proposal for a data center adjacent to established residential and agricultural uses.

timeline.title: Planning Commission recommends denial
timeline.summary: The commission recommended against the rezoning after extensive written opposition and public concern.

timeline.title: City Council unanimously denies rezoning
timeline.summary: Council denied the application 7–0 after public testimony, citing incompatibility with the location and community.

timeline.title: City adopts a broader data-center ordinance
timeline.summary: The city later adopted an ordinance governing future data-center siting. This is tracked as a policy consequence, not an economic effect of the rejected parcel.

projects.name: Project Accelerate
projects.decision_label: Rezoning petition withdrawn before scheduled vote
projects.summary: Developers withdrew the five-building Project Accelerate rezoning after sustained public opposition and an indication that town commissioners would reject it.
projects.proposal_description: The proposal sought industrial rezoning for a multi-building data-center campus on East John Street near Interstate 485 in Matthews.

proposed_scale.label: Proposed electricity request
proposed_scale.value: Up to 600 MW reported; not built capacity

projects.site_afterlife: The withdrawal left options open. No stable alternative use or sufficiently long post-period is established in this release.
projects.evidence_note: Recent disposition; map and timeline eligible, economic comparison not ready. The developer described the withdrawal as allowing time to explore options.

projects.name: Harper Road Technology Park
projects.decision_label: Board removed data centers from the zoning code
projects.summary: Peculiar reversed its zoning approach and removed data centers as a permitted use after organized local opposition, blocking Diode Ventures' planned Harper Road campus.
projects.proposal_description: Diode Ventures discussed a hyperscale technology park near Harper Road. The city's review moved from enabling language to a moratorium and then removal of data centers from the zoning code.
projects.site_afterlife: No verified replacement use for the proposed site is included. Citywide zoning treatment should be tracked separately from parcel-level economic outcomes.
projects.evidence_note: The policy action is verified in the city's agenda packet. The causal link to one developer's final investment decision requires continued company and parcel research.

projects.name: Bolingbroke Technology Center
projects.summary: Monroe County's planning board and County Commission unanimously rejected rezoning for the proposed Bolingbroke campus after large public turnout. Later litigation prevents treatment as a settled final outcome.
projects.proposal_description: The application sought commercial rezoning for a large, multi-building technology campus on mostly undeveloped land near U.S. 41, Wadley Road, and I-475.
projects.site_afterlife: The denial was followed by litigation reported against the county. Until the legal and parcel status are resolved, no stable post-decision economic comparison should be made.
projects.evidence_note: Disposition verified, but litigation makes the treatment date and finality unsuitable for causal modeling.
